newsitem.title: PERU: Peru's Fujimori flies to Germany to promote image.
newsitem.headline: Peru's Fujimori flies to Germany to promote image.

text.p: President Alberto Fujimori left on Monday for a four-day trip to Germany to promote Peru's image and attract investment, government officials said.

A high-level delegation that includes Economy Minister Jorge Camet, Labour Minister Jorge Gonzalez Izquierdo, Foreign Minister Francisco Tudela, congressmen and business leaders was accompanying Fujimori to help woo investors, they said.

Fujimori was to meet with Germany's Chancellor Helmut Kohl during the visit, which comes just days after Peruvian novelist Mario Vargas Llosa made a scathing attack on Fujimori in Germany. At a ceremony to receive the German book industry's prestigious Peace Prize, Vargas Llosa accused the international community of indifference to human rights abuses under Fujimori's rule.

Since taking power in 1990, Fujimori has stabilised the country's economy and made Peru attractive to foreign investors. But his authoritarian style has led to criticism that the government restricts democratic institutions and allows human rights abuses.
